question: How does previous practice lead one to yoga and transcend word-Brahman?
premises: By previous practice one is carried, even unwilling.
Even one desirous of knowing yoga transcends word-Brahman.
Indeed, even unwilling and dependent, by that previous practice alone one is led by force toward yoga practice.
Mere inquiry into yoga alone does not transcend word-Brahman.
Word-Brahman in the form of mantra-study and the like is not transcended but taken up.
inference: Previous practice forcibly carries one into yoga practice and enables transcendence of word-Brahman, whereas mere yoga inquiry does not transcend but takes up word-Brahman.
uncertainties: The exact force of svīkurute is unclear: it may mean 'takes up' or 'accepts/adopts.'
The relation between 'transcends word-Brahman' and 'takes up word-Brahman' is not fully resolved by the gloss.
plain_english: By previous practice one is carried even unwilling; even one desiring to know yoga transcends word-Brahman. Indeed, even unwilling and dependent, by that previous practice alone one is forcibly led to yoga practice. This is not ordinary: mere inquiry into yoga alone does not transcend word-Brahman; word-Brahman in the form of mantra-study and the like is not transcended but taken up.
